dimensions.rationale: Implements metrics, trend, segments, anomalies/events, states, and period selection, but objective coverage is weakened by populated/partial gate failures and missing automated screenshots for those states.
Provides the fuller task flow with period selection, anomaly detail, and segment inspection, but mobile wrapping/clipping and failed objective evidence reduce confidence.
Dense operational layout and tables fit the brief, but mobile composition degrades and some content becomes cramped.
Queue/detail/segment-table structure is more product-specific than a plain KPI wall, though styling remains conventional SaaS dashboard language.
Has labels and focus styles, but serious axe failures occur in populated and partial states: invalid definition-list structure and non-focusable scrollable region.
Manual populated/partial captures are reviewable, but objective gate is only 20/28 and narrow viewport evidence shows cramped layout plus scrollable-region-focusable failures.
All required states exist and partial data is modeled, but partial/populated objective runs fail and empty state is comparatively sparse.
Tokens and component styling are consistent, but semantic markup defects in the metric region weaken design-system rigor.
Includes build/serve/verify scripts and period state handling, but direct fixture HTML insertion patterns and accessibility-breaking markup are maintainability risks.
Static dependency-free implementation with no heavy runtime assets observed.
Period changes, missing comparison, delayed data, and no anomalies are represented, but mobile clipping and failed partial gates reduce stress-case fidelity.
Uses deterministic local fixture data and no live commercial data dependency is visible.
Build/test scripts exist, but objective gate is 20/28 with serious populated/partial accessibility failures; run record also notes a dev-server sandbox failure.

uncertainty: Manual populated/partial screenshots prove renderability, but missing automated screenshots for those states are treated as uncertainty, not success.
conclusion: Candidate B has a broader workflow, especially period selection, but the 20/28 objective gate result and serious accessibility failures materially lower the score.
